headline_en: Rajbari's Azad, who went to Iraq to restore his family's fortunes, is murdered there
summary_en: Azad Ali Khan (47), a clothing trader and tailor from Goalanda, Rajbari, went to Iraq on 24 June 2025 through his cousin Babul Khan, an Iraq-based expatriate, after paying BDT 725,000. He was left at a hotel in Baghdad without the promised job, later took work in a house, was not paid for over three months, and was killed by the house owner on 12 September 2025 after a pay dispute; his dismembered body was found in a drain on 18 September. The house owner surrendered to police and confessed.

facts.statement: Azad Ali Khan (47) of Goalanda, Rajbari spent BDT 725,000 (7 lakh 25 thousand taka), raised through borrowing, to go to Iraq on 24 June 2025 through his cousin Babul Khan, a Bangladeshi living in Iraq.
facts.source_in_article: Azad's relatives and his wife Sharmin Begum

facts.statement: Azad Ali Khan was promised a well-paid job in Iraq, but after arriving at Kazumia (কাজুমিয়া) in Baghdad his cousin Babul Khan, who had taken him there, left him at a hotel and went away; he got no job and stayed unemployed.
After a few days in the Baghdad hotel Azad Ali Khan took work in a private house; after more than three months of work the house owner had not paid his wages, which led to a dispute.

On 12 September 2025, during an argument over unpaid wages, the house owner (described by a relative as his kafil) killed Azad Ali Khan in Baghdad, cut the body into three pieces according to the cousin Babul, and dumped it in a nearby drain.
facts.source_in_article: Azad's relatives; brother-in-law Anwar Hossain quoting Babul Khan

facts.statement: Six days after the killing, on Thursday 18 September 2025, cleaners smelled the body in the drain and told police, who recovered the dismembered body; the house owner then surrendered at the police station himself and confessed to killing Azad.
In about four months in Iraq Azad Ali Khan was able to send home only BDT 60,000 in total, his wife said, because he could not get work.

After reporting the death by phone at about 2 am, the cousin Babul Khan, who had taken Azad to Iraq, could not be reached properly by the family; the family said they did not know what to do next. The wife last spoke to Azad on the night of 11 September, when he said he was not well.
facts.source_in_article: wife Sharmin Begum and brother-in-law Anwar Hossain

named_actors.location: Iraq (cousin of the victim, from Goalanda, Rajbari)

headline_en: Every expatriate's life is a novel
summary_en: A first-person 'Dur Porobash' reader column by a Bangladeshi doctor on training at a Paris hospital describes the lives of Bangladeshis he met there. One waited 12 years in Europe for a residence card without visiting home; another reached Paris via Libya and a Mediterranean boat to Italy and has worked 14 hours a day at a kebab shop for seven years; a third paid BDT 10 lakh to reach Cyprus and another BDT 10 lakh to reach Paris and is jobless, selling roasted corn for 5 to 10 euros profit a day.

facts.statement: A Bangladeshi named Azad in Paris came to Europe on a programme and stayed on, applied for permanent status and expected a residence card ('sthayikoron card') in two or three years, but waited more than 12 years; he said that leaving Europe without the card would mean he could not come back, so he did not visit Bangladesh for 12 years. He received the card about 15 days before the column was written and was going home.

Giasuddin from Sylhet reached Paris via Libya: in Libya the smuggler ('adam bepari') kept him confined in one room for a month with one piece of bread and one cup of water a day, then sent him across the Mediterranean towards Italy.

On Giasuddin's Mediterranean crossing from Libya, 80 people were put on one plastic boat at night and one of the passengers was made the boatman; the trip was supposed to reach Italy after one day but the boatman lost the way and after two days no land was seen. A cargo ship found them adrift and handed them to the Italian coastguard. Three other boats left with them and Giasuddin later learned that one sank at sea.

Giasuddin has worked for seven years at a kebab shop in Paris grilling about 300 chickens a day over wood fire, working 14 hours a day (leaving at 8 am and returning at midnight), and sends almost his whole monthly pay to Bangladesh.
Giasuddin did not visit Bangladesh for seven years while waiting for a residence card; about a month before the column he was given status in Paris for one year and planned to go home in September.
A Bangladeshi man selling roasted corn beside a Paris metro station said he spent BDT 10 lakh to go to Cyprus, worked there two years and sent some money home, then lost his job.
The same man, unable to do anything in Cyprus, paid another BDT 10 lakh to come to Paris; seven months after arriving he had no job.

The jobless Bangladeshi in Paris said his room rent is 150 euros and food costs about 100 euros (the article does not state the period); he sells roasted corn on a fellow Bangladeshi's advice and makes 5 to 10 euros profit a day, sends nothing home, and says fellow Bangladeshis no longer help him.

The columnist writes that his plan to stay in a hotel for a few days in Paris and then look for a rented room would have been 'a big mistake', as he understood after arriving; he was housed through a Bangladeshi contact arranged before travel.

The columnist says expatriates often do not get the benefit of the money they send: relatives take it, and when they return in old age they find the property registered in others' names and nothing in their own.

headline_en: Admission to Korean language course in Dhaka, applications close 26 August
summary_en: Dhaka Mohila (Women's) Technical Training Centre opened admission to the ninth batch of its four-month Korean language course for the September to December 2025 session, run by BMET under the expatriates' welfare ministry. There are 40 seats for women or men, the admission fee is BDT 1,000, and applications closed on 26 August 2025.

facts.statement: Dhaka Mohila Technical Training Centre (ঢাকা মহিলা কারিগরি প্রশিক্ষণকেন্দ্র) runs a four-month Korean language training course, ninth batch, September to December 2025, under the Ministry of Expatriates' Welfare and Overseas Employment and conducted by the Bureau of Manpower, Employment and Training (BMET); 40 seats for women or men; a government certificate is given at the end.
The admission fee for the BMET Korean language course at Dhaka Mohila Technical Training Centre is BDT 1,000.
Eligibility for the Korean language course at Dhaka Mohila Technical Training Centre: at least SSC or equivalent pass, age 18 to 35.

Documents to submit with the application for the Korean language course: two recent passport-size photos, a photocopy of the national ID or birth registration, and photocopies of all educational certificates.

Schedule for the Korean language course at Dhaka Mohila Technical Training Centre: applications submitted by 26 August 2025, 9:30 am to 3:30; selection (physical fitness and oral test) on 27 August 2025 from 10 am, with priority to those who hold a passport; result on 28 August 2025; admission 31 August to 1 September 2025 at the training branch; training starts 3 September 2025 (printed as Sunday) in room 306.

headline_en: Admission to Japanese language course in Chattogram, fee only one thousand taka
summary_en: The government Bangladesh-Korea Technical Training Centre (BK-TTC) in Chattogram opened admission to a four-month Japanese language course (Level N4 / JFT Basic Test) for September to December 2025 under BMET, designed for workers who want to go to Japan. There are 30 seats, the assessment fee is BDT 1,000, and applicants need SSC plus a Level N5 pass; applications closed on 26 August 2025.

facts.statement: Bangladesh-Korea Technical Training Centre (BK-TTC), Chattogram, runs a four-month Japanese language course (Level N4 / JFT Basic Test) in the September to December 2025 session under BMET of the Ministry of Expatriates' Welfare and Overseas Employment, made specially for workers wishing to go to Japan; 30 seats.
The course assessment fee for the BK-TTC Chattogram Japanese N4/JFT Basic course is BDT 1,000; the end-of-course assessment is done by BMET.
Eligibility for the BK-TTC Chattogram Japanese N4/JFT Basic course: at least SSC or equivalent and a pass in Japanese language Level N5; age 17 to 35; physically in good health.

Knowing Japanese is compulsory for employment in Japan, and to go to Japan as a Specified Skilled Worker (SSW) a person must have passed at least Japanese language Level N4 / JFT Basic Test, according to the BK-TTC course notice.
The BK-TTC notice says Japan will recruit a large number of Specified Skilled Workers (SSW) from various countries including Bangladesh.
Applicants for the BK-TTC Japanese course collect the application form from the TTC or download the prescribed admission form from the BMET website, fill it in and submit it within the deadline.

Schedule for the BK-TTC Chattogram Japanese course: applications until 26 August 2025; selection/admission test 27 August 2025 at 10 am; result 28 August 2025; admission from the merit list until 28 August 2025 and from the waiting list on 31 August 2025; classes start 1 September 2025 from 8 am.

headline_en: Property worth BDT 500 crore of manpower-export 'syndicate chief' Ruhul seized
summary_en: Police CID said on Wednesday 20 August 2025 that it had attached about BDT 500 crore of property belonging to Ruhul Amin (Swapan), described as chief of the syndicate for sending workers to Malaysia, and connected persons and entities, on an order of the Dhaka Metropolitan Sessions Judge's Court. CID says the syndicate embezzled BDT 8,000 crore and that inquiries into other syndicate members continue.

facts.statement: CID announced on 20 August 2025 that property worth about BDT 500 crore of Ruhul Amin (Swapan), described as chief of the Malaysia manpower-export syndicate, and of persons and entities linked to him has been seized/attached; the Dhaka Metropolitan Sessions Judge's Court issued the order on an application by the inquiry officer of CID's Financial Crime division.
facts.source_in_article: CID Special Superintendent of Police (Media) Jasim Uddin Khan, press release

facts.statement: CID says Ruhul Amin, as chief of a syndicate formed for sending workers to Malaysia, embezzled BDT 8,000 crore, bought houses and land with it, and thereby also committed money laundering.

Ruhul Amin's recruiting firm Catharsis International holds 231 katha of land under seven deeds in Bashundhara Residential Area, Banani and Uttara in Dhaka, with a deed value of BDT 15 crore 55 lakh 33 thousand; that land, the Catharsis International establishment on it and various structures, together valued at BDT 500 crore of immovable property, have been attached.

CID says inquiries are continuing against the other members of the Malaysia manpower-export syndicate as well as Ruhul Amin, and action under the money laundering law will be taken against the others too.

headline_en: How students going abroad can get certificates attested online
summary_en: An explainer (source: UNB) on the government's online attestation service for educational certificates and transcripts for people going abroad, available on the MyGov platform, which the article says started on 'last 1 October' so applicants no longer need to go to the Ministry of Education. It walks through registration, profile verification with NID or birth registration, finding the service, filling the form, uploading scans, paying any fee, tracking, and downloading the attested document.

facts.date: since 1 October (article published 3 July 2025 says 'last 1 October'; year not stated)
facts.statement: The Bangladesh government runs an online service for attesting educational certificates and academic transcripts for people going abroad; applicants no longer have to go to the Ministry of Education for attestation.

For online attestation of education documents on MyGov, the only identity document needed is the national ID (NID) or an online-registered birth registration certificate; documents must be scanned beforehand and saved as JPEG, JPG or PNG files of no more than 1 MB each.

Step 1 of online attestation: open an account on the MyGov platform with name and mobile number or email address and set a password; then verify the profile immediately with NID or birth registration number and birth year. One NID can verify only one MyGov account.

On the MyGov homepage the first listed service is 'বিদেশগামী নাগরিকদের সার্টিফিকেট সত্যায়ন' (certificate attestation for citizens going abroad); clicking it shows separate application options for each type of document, and a specific document can also be found through the homepage search box, including by voice command.

Each MyGov attestation application option lists the documents needed, upload rules, the application fee, how to fill the online form and the processing time; these differ by document type, some services are free and others carry a set fee, payable by online banking, card or mobile payment gateway.

In the MyGov attestation form, fields marked with a red star are mandatory and others may be left blank; a plus (+) button adds multiple pages or files; a partly filled application can be saved as a draft and resumed later from the 'সেবা ব্যবস্থাপনা' (service management) option after logging in with mobile number or email and password.

Documents can be uploaded to the MyGov account once, right after account verification, and are then attached automatically to later applications; an applicant cannot go to the next step until attachments have fully uploaded.

After final submission each MyGov attestation application gets a unique tracking number; its status can be checked from the 'সেবা ব্যবস্থাপনা' option and the personal dashboard. After the set number of working days the attested document appears on the dashboard and can be downloaded.

headline_en: Balance of payments improves on the back of exports and remittances
summary_en: Bangladesh Bank data show the overall balance of payments deficit fell to USD 66 crore at the end of July to April of fiscal year 2024-25, helped by strong growth in goods exports and remittances. Remittances in July to April were USD 2,454 crore, 28 percent higher than a year earlier, and reserves rose.

facts.statement: Remittances to Bangladesh in July to April of fiscal year 2024-25 were USD 2,454 crore, 28 percent more than in the same period of the previous fiscal year.
After April, a record amount of remittances also came in May 2025, according to economists and Bangladesh Bank officials.

On 29 May 2025 Bangladesh's foreign exchange reserves were USD 25.80 billion by Bangladesh Bank's own method and USD 2,057 crore by the IMF's BPM6 method; a year earlier the BPM6 figure was USD 1,872 crore, so usable reserves rose USD 185 crore in a year.

Bangladesh's overall balance of payments deficit fell to USD 66 crore at the end of July to April of FY2024-25, from USD 107 crore a month earlier and USD 557 crore at end April of the previous fiscal year; the current account deficit fell to USD 139 crore, from USD 661 crore for all of FY2023-24.
In May 2025 the dollar exchange rate in Bangladesh was left to the market; officials said it stayed stable because supply was good.

headline_en: The 'vision' of a society without discrimination is missing from the budget: Nahid
summary_en: At a press conference on Tuesday 3 June 2025, National Citizen Party (NCP) convener Nahid Islam gave the party's reaction to the interim government's budget, saying it lacks a vision of economic transformation and measures on unemployment. He condemned what he described as the halving of the expatriates' welfare ministry's budget.

facts.statement: NCP convener Nahid Islam said the proposed national budget cut the Expatriates' Welfare Ministry's budget by half; he condemned the cut, saying it makes unclear what the government is doing for migrant workers, and that his party had asked for institutional skills training for people going abroad.
facts.source_in_article: Nahid Islam, convener, National Citizen Party, at a press conference in Banglamotor, Dhaka

facts.statement: Nahid Islam said the number of unemployed people in Bangladesh rose by 26 lakh in the past year and that the budget has no policy to raise investment for job creation.

headline_en: After a year in a Saudi ICU, Rajshahi's Jabbar opens his eyes once brought home
summary_en: Abdul Jabbar Sardar (45) of Tanore, Rajshahi, who went to Saudi Arabia in January 2018 for BDT 7 lakh, was badly injured in a road accident on 10 May 2024 and lay in a Saudi hospital ICU for over a year. After his wife applied in writing to the Wage Earners' Welfare Board in January 2025 and the Board wrote to the embassy, he was flown home unconscious on 23 May 2025 and is now in Rajshahi Medical College Hospital. The Board says the family can apply for treatment assistance of up to BDT 1.5 lakh if he is a registered worker.

facts.statement: Abdul Jabbar Sardar, a farmer from Hiranandapur village, Tanore, Rajshahi, raised BDT 7 lakh through borrowing and went to Saudi Arabia on 16 January 2018.

On landing at the airport in Saudi Arabia Jabbar was put to work as a cleaner; he understood that the brokers had 'sold' him as an airport cleaner. After three years he was sent away from the airport job empty-handed.
After three years of airport cleaning work in Saudi Arabia Abdul Jabbar Sardar was dismissed with nothing in hand; he later got work at another establishment through a man from his home area.

Abdul Jabbar Sardar was seriously injured in a road accident in Saudi Arabia on 10 May 2024; Saudi law enforcement rescued him and admitted him to a local hospital, where he remained in the ICU for more than a year; a tracheostomy tube was inserted there.
facts.source_in_article: wife Adori Khatun; Abu Hena Mostafa Kamal, ICU in-charge, Rajshahi Medical College Hospital

facts.statement: The Wage Earners' Welfare Board has a programme to bring a migrant worker back to Bangladesh by contacting the embassy, on an application from the worker or the worker's family.

Jabbar's wife applied in writing to the Director General of the Wage Earners' Welfare Board on 13 January 2025 and visited the Board's Rajshahi Welfare Centre day after day; the Board wrote to the embassy about repatriating him and sent a reminder letter on 9 April 2025; he was sent back and arrived in Bangladesh unconscious at dawn on 23 May 2025.
facts.source_in_article: wife Adori Khatun; Main Uddin, Assistant Director (Information and Public Relations), Wage Earners' Welfare Board

facts.statement: The Wage Earners' Welfare Board said the family of the returned injured worker can now apply for treatment assistance, and if he is a registered worker the Board can give up to BDT 1.5 lakh (one and a half lakh taka) quickly.
facts.source_in_article: Main Uddin, Assistant Director (Information and Public Relations), Wage Earners' Welfare Board

facts.statement: After return Jabbar was first kept in a hospital in Dhaka, but the family could not afford it and moved him to Rajshahi Medical College Hospital, where he was admitted to the ICU on 26 May 2025 and moved to a general ward on 31 May 2025; the ICU in-charge said he is emaciated, needs nutrition and a head operation, and may then regain consciousness.
facts.source_in_article: wife Adori Khatun; ICU in-charge Abu Hena Mostafa Kamal

named_actors.name: Wage Earners' Welfare Board (Rajshahi Welfare Centre)
named_actors.what_the_article_says: Received the family's written application in January 2025, wrote to the embassy and sent a reminder on 9 April 2025; says up to BDT 1.5 lakh treatment assistance is available for a registered worker. Spokesman: Assistant Director Main Uddin.

people_cases.who: Abdul Jabbar Sardar, 45, Hiranandapur village, Tanore upazila, Rajshahi
people_cases.what_happened: Went on 16 January 2018; put to work as an airport cleaner, 'sold' by brokers; dismissed empty-handed after three years; found another job; seriously injured in a road accident on 10 May 2024 and spent over a year in a Saudi ICU.
people_cases.outcome: Repatriated unconscious on 23 May 2025 after the wife's application to the Wage Earners' Welfare Board; in Rajshahi Medical College Hospital, opened one eye; family may apply for up to BDT 1.5 lakh treatment aid.

headline_en: 'I was beaten on a false theft charge and then they tried to kill me by throwing me off the train'
summary_en: Motiur Rahman (40), who runs a manpower-export business from Raninagar, Naogaon, says seven masked youths beat him on a Santahar-bound train on Sunday 18 May 2025 and pushed him off, over a dispute with the family of Sajib, a man he sent to Saudi Arabia who has not got work or an iqama. He filed an attempted-murder case at Santahar Junction GRP police station on 19 May naming Sumon, Sajib's brother-in-law; Sajib's father denies involvement.

facts.statement: Sajib of Talson village, Adamdighi, Bogura was sent to Saudi Arabia through Motiur Rahman about 40 days before 20 May 2025 and had still not got any work, his father said; the father said Motiur avoided meeting the family and was hiding in various places.

The police case statement (FIR) says that after Sajib went to Saudi Arabia through Motiur Rahman 'some days ago', problems in his papers meant he did not get an iqama, which caused the dispute between Sajib's family and Motiur.
facts.source_in_article: case FIR filed by Motiur Rahman

facts.statement: Motiur Rahman (40) of Paroil Fakirpara village, Raninagar, Naogaon, who does manpower-export business, says seven masked youths beat him on a train after Altafnagar station on 18 May 2025, accused him of stealing two mobile phones, and pushed him from the moving train; he hung from the door rod for four to five minutes until Nasratpur station and fell under the train, surviving with injuries.

Motiur Rahman filed an attempted-murder case at Santahar Junction GRP police station on the night of 19 May 2025, naming Sumon (30), son of Sirajul Islam of Daharpur/Doharpur village, Adamdighi, Bogura (brother-in-law of Saudi migrant Sajib) as main accused, plus six or seven unnamed others; the OC said raids to arrest the accused were under way.
facts.source_in_article: Santahar Railway police station OC Habibur Rahman; the case record

headline_en: What is known about the viral video of a man being thrown from a moving train
summary_en: A 35-second viral video shows a man hanging from and falling off a moving train near Nasratpur station, Adamdighi, Bogura on Sunday 18 May 2025. The victim is Motiur Rahman (52 in this report), described by family sources as a manpower broker ('adam byabsayi'), who was allegedly attacked over a dispute with the family of Sajib, whom he sent to Saudi Arabia and who has not received an iqama. Sajib's uncle accuses Motiur of cheating but denies any role in the attack.

facts.statement: Sajib of Talson village, Adamdighi, Bogura went to Saudi Arabia through Motiur Rahman (this article says two years ago); because of problems in his papers he has not received an iqama, and the company he was sent to work for has still not given one.
facts.source_in_article: family sources; Jahangir Alam, uncle of Sajib

facts.statement: Sajib's uncle says Motiur Rahman cheated his nephew: Motiur promised to get him an iqama in Saudi Arabia and keeps making excuses while saying he will provide it.

Motiur Rahman (52) of Paroil village, Raninagar, Naogaon, described as an 'adam byabsayi' (manpower broker), was beaten by 10 to 12 youths on the Dolonchapa Express from Bogura to Santahar at about 1 pm on 18 May 2025 and pushed from the moving train near Nasratpur station; one leg was broken, his son said.

Motiur's son said Adamdighi police station referred the family to Santahar GRP police station, which also did not take a case on the night of 18 May 2025; the GRP inspector said nobody had come with a complaint and action would follow an investigation if one was received.
facts.source_in_article: son Ahsan Habib; Santahar GRP inspector Habibur Rahman

headline_en: Fees for English-medium exams can be sent abroad through exam centres: Bangladesh Bank
summary_en: Bangladesh Bank issued an order on Monday 21 April 2025 allowing banks to remit abroad, without its prior approval, fees for O Level, A Level and AS Level exams held in Bangladesh and for tests such as TOEFL and SAT. Authorised exam centres may collect the admission and exam fees in taka and banks remit against invoices.

facts.statement: Under a Bangladesh Bank order issued on 21 April 2025, authorised exam centres may collect admission and exam-related fees in taka for O Level, A Level/AS Level and tests such as TOEFL and SAT, and the fees can be sent abroad through the centres; the centres must be duly approved by the foreign authority concerned.

Banks in Bangladesh can now remit fees for TOEFL, SAT and similar tests and for secondary/higher-secondary equivalent foreign exams held in Bangladesh without Bangladesh Bank's approval, which was previously required; banks remit on the basis of an invoice and a detailed statement, and must take a declaration and undertaking from the exam centre before the remittance.

headline_en: Yasin joined the Russian army to fulfil his father's dream
summary_en: Yasin Mia Sheikh (22) of Gouripur, Mymensingh left for Russia on 4 September 2024 on a job arranged through a firm in Uttara, worked three months, then voluntarily signed up online as a contract fighter in the Russian army on 22 December 2024. He was killed in a Ukrainian missile strike on 27 March 2025; the family, which spent BDT 15 lakh from land sale and loans, learned of it on 1 April and has applied through the administration for the body.

facts.statement: Yasin Mia Sheikh's elder brother Ruhul Amin provided BDT 15 lakh for his journey to Russia: BDT 7 lakh from selling 40 decimals of family land and BDT 8 lakh in loans.

Yasin Mia Sheikh said in a Facebook video that he interviewed with a Chinese company in January 2024, received an offer letter in September 2024 for a job about 11,000 km from Moscow, worked in Russia for three months and then voluntarily joined the Russian army through an online process; before leaving on 4 September 2024 he had said he was going through a firm in Uttara, Dhaka (not named).
facts.source_in_article: Yasin Mia Sheikh's own Facebook videos, as reported

The family of the Bangladeshi killed fighting for Russia applied in writing through the local administration to get the body back; the Gouripur Upazila Nirbahi Officer said an Assistant Commissioner (Land) was sent to the home on Thursday 3 April 2025 and the application would be forwarded to the proper government authority.

headline_en: Air ticket bookings cannot be held for more than three days
summary_en: The Ministry of Civil Aviation and Tourism has issued ten directives, gazetted on 18 February 2025, to curb abnormal rises in air ticket prices. Airlines may not hold a booking for more than three days (72 hours) without issuing the ticket in the passenger's name with passport details, group-booked blocked tickets must be sold within seven days, all tickets must be sold online with the price shown, and Biman and others were told to act to cut fares for migrant workers going to the Middle East and Malaysia.

facts.statement: No airline in Bangladesh may hold an air ticket booking for more than three days (72 hours): a booked ticket must be issued in the passenger's name within three days, the booking must be made with the passenger's name, passport number and passport photocopy, and a booking not ticketed within three days must be cancelled automatically.
facts.source_in_article: Ministry of Civil Aviation and Tourism directive

facts.statement: Tickets that airlines and travel agencies had blocked through group booking before the directive must be sold in the names of specific passengers within seven days, failing which they are cancelled automatically within the following three days.
facts.source_in_article: Ministry of Civil Aviation and Tourism

facts.statement: For group bookings the actual sale price of each ticket must be reported to the civil aviation ministry at the time of sale and the ministry will publish it on its website; all air tickets must be sold online, with the price shown online and on the ticket.
facts.source_in_article: Ministry of Civil Aviation and Tourism directive

facts.statement: If a travel agency stockpiles more tickets than demand and sells them through other agents so that prices rise, the original travel agency's registration certificate will be cancelled or suspended.
facts.source_in_article: Ministry of Civil Aviation and Tourism directive

facts.statement: The civil aviation ministry directed Biman Bangladesh Airlines and others concerned to take the necessary steps to reduce ticket fares for migrant workers going abroad, including to the Middle East and Malaysia; no fare figure is given.
facts.source_in_article: Ministry of Civil Aviation and Tourism directive

headline_en: Service seekers allege they are sent back repeatedly and forced to use brokers
summary_en: An inquiry committee of the Department of Immigration and Passports heard 15 to 16 complainants at Rajshahi Circuit House on Monday 17 February 2025 about bribe-taking at the Rajshahi Regional Passport Office. Complainants described being turned back over invented errors until they paid BDT 2,000 to BDT 20,000 through intermediaries, with Ansar members said to fix everything; the deputy director, Rozy Khondoker, declined to comment before the inquiry report.

facts.statement: At Rajshahi Regional Passport Office, complainants told an inquiry that applicants with correct papers are shown false errors and sent back repeatedly until they go to a broker; Ansar members there 'solve all problems', and those who pay a bribe through a broker are served first while the queue stays where it is. One complainant claimed 98 percent of people have to pay bribes there.
facts.source_in_article: a complainant (social worker) before the inquiry committee

facts.statement: A woman told the inquiry her passport form at Rajshahi Regional Passport Office was rejected for an error at the start and the deputy director gave no solution; she paid a BDT 2,000 bribe through an intermediary, was sent straight to the photo room, and the same form was accepted.
facts.source_in_article: a woman complainant before the inquiry committee

facts.statement: The nephew of a Rajshahi city BNP leader said his uncle, who has a court case against him, submitted the court's permission with the passport application, but the file was held for three months by the deputy director; after a BDT 20,000 bribe paid through an intermediary the passport was issued within 15 days.
facts.source_in_article: nephew of a Rajshahi city BNP leader, before the inquiry committee

facts.statement: A pharmacy owner in Rajshahi city told the inquiry he paid a BDT 2,000 bribe through an intermediary, after which his passport was corrected.
facts.source_in_article: a pharmacy owner before the inquiry committee

facts.statement: The Department of Immigration and Passports formed an inquiry committee after victims held a human chain on 20 November against corruption at Rajshahi passport office and deputy director Rozy Khondoker filed a police complaint against protesters; on 17 February 2025, from 11 am to 5 pm at Rajshahi Circuit House, director A K M Mazharul Islam and assistant director Moinul Hossain took written and oral statements from 15 to 16 complainants and will submit a report.
facts.source_in_article: A K M Mazharul Islam, Director, Department of Immigration and Passports

facts.statement: Many complainants said Rajshahi passport office deputy director Rozy Khondoker is reluctant to let service seekers into her room and makes everyone, including sick people, stand in front of her desk; she said she would respond after seeing the inquiry report.

headline_en: Government issues 10 directives to control air ticket prices
summary_en: On Tuesday 11 February 2025 the Ministry of Civil Aviation and Tourism issued a circular with ten directives, effective immediately, to stop abnormal rises in air ticket prices. They cover named bookings with passport copies, automatic cancellation after 72 hours, release of blocked group tickets, online sale with printed prices, tariff filing, a ban on selling above approved fares and through unregistered agencies, and special fares for outbound workers.

facts.statement: Directive 1: any ticket reservation in Bangladesh, including group bookings, must have the passenger's name, passport number and passport photocopy attached; if the ticket is not issued in that passenger's name within three days of booking it is cancelled automatically after 72 hours.
facts.source_in_article: Ministry of Civil Aviation and Tourism circular

facts.statement: Directive 2: tickets blocked by airlines or travel agencies through group booking up to the date of the circular must be sold with passenger name, passport number and passport copy within seven days; otherwise the airline cancels them automatically within the next three days.
facts.source_in_article: Ministry of Civil Aviation and Tourism circular

facts.statement: Directives 3 and 4: for group bookings the real ticket price must be reported to the Ministry of Civil Aviation and Tourism as soon as the ticket is sold and will be published on a website; all air tickets must be available for sale online and the price must be stated online and on the ticket.
facts.source_in_article: Ministry of Civil Aviation and Tourism circular

facts.statement: Directives 5 and 6: airlines and travel agencies must follow tariff filing under the Civil Aviation Rules 1984 and publish the tariff approved by the Civil Aviation Authority of Bangladesh (CAAB/Bebichak) on a website; no airline or travel agency may sell a ticket above the CAAB-approved fare, and travel agencies must give the passenger the ticket at the airline-set price and a sales receipt.
facts.source_in_article: Ministry of Civil Aviation and Tourism circular

facts.statement: Directive 7: if a travel agency hoards extra tickets without need and sells them through other agents so that the price rises, its registration certificate will be suspended or cancelled.
facts.source_in_article: Ministry of Civil Aviation and Tourism circular

facts.statement: Directives 8 and 9: airlines operating flights in Bangladesh and travel agencies are to arrange special air fares for workers going abroad, and Biman Bangladesh Airlines, all airlines and the Board of Airlines Representatives (BAR) are to take the necessary steps within seven days to reduce ticket fares for migrant workers to the Middle East, Malaysia and elsewhere; no fare amount is stated.
facts.source_in_article: Ministry of Civil Aviation and Tourism circular

facts.statement: Directive 10: ticket sales through travel agencies not registered under the Bangladesh Travel Agency (Registration and Control) Act 2013 must be stopped.
facts.source_in_article: Ministry of Civil Aviation and Tourism circular

headline_en: Demand for jobs for expatriates harmed over the mass uprising
summary_en: At a press conference at the National Press Club on Friday 7 February 2025, returnees under the banner 'expatriates from the United Arab Emirates and elsewhere' made six demands, including jobs and a trust like the July Shaheed Smriti Foundation for expatriates who were arrested and sent back after protesting abroad in support of the July-August 2024 movement. They alleged that the then consul general in the UAE passed protesters' details to Emirati law enforcement. The article recalls that the UAE jailed 57 Bangladeshis for protesting and later pardoned them and 75 more.

facts.statement: A court in the United Arab Emirates sentenced 57 Bangladeshis to prison terms of various lengths for demonstrating in the UAE in solidarity with Bangladesh's quota reform movement; the UAE government later pardoned them after efforts by Bangladesh's interim government.
Towards the end of November 2024 the UAE government pardoned a further 75 detained Bangladeshi expatriates.

Returnees alleged that some people handed the addresses and passport numbers of Bangladeshis who protested in the UAE and other countries to the consular office, that the then Consul General in the UAE, B M Jamal, sent the information to that country's law enforcement, that Awami League leaders prepared lists of protesters and critics, and that expatriates in the UAE were arrested on that basis; they demanded those responsible be identified and tried.

headline_en: Why has the Saudi Arabia air fare risen so much, asks Rashed Khan
summary_en: At a human chain held by Bangladesh Probashi Odhikar Parishad in front of the National Press Club on Thursday 6 February 2025 against abnormal air ticket price rises, Gono Odhikar Parishad general secretary Rashed Khan asked why fares to Saudi Arabia had risen so much. Speakers demanded fares be brought to a reasonable level within seven days, removal of travel tax and other charges, more flights and a regulatory board.

facts.statement: Bangladesh Probashi Odhikar Parishad said ticket prices on flights from Bangladesh to the Middle East, Asia and Europe had reached an extreme level, and that because of the excess fares many workers were unable to go abroad, hurting their livelihoods and remittance inflow. No fare figures are given.

facts.statement: Demands at the human chain: bring air ticket prices to a reasonable level within seven days; increase flights by Bangladesh Biman and other domestic and international airlines; form a regulatory board to keep ticket prices stable; and withdraw travel tax, excise duty, landing and parking charges and all unnecessary charges.

headline_en: Theft in the banking sector was encouraged from the highest level: Foreign Adviser
summary_en: Opening the integrated online attestation system (first step of implementing the Apostille Convention 1961) on Wednesday 29 January 2025, Foreign Adviser Md. Touhid Hossain said 60,000 Bangladeshi passports are stuck in Italy because of doubts about the credibility of documents. He also spoke of manpower shortages at missions, citing Qatar, said a decision has been made to increase mission staff, and of the image cost of Bangladeshis being the largest group among those drowning in the Mediterranean.

facts.statement: Foreign Adviser Md. Touhid Hossain said 60,000 Bangladeshi passports are stuck in Italy because of doubts over the credibility of documents; he said every case has some problem, for example a Bangladeshi broker obtained an approval from a company there that in reality is in no position to employ the person.

The Foreign Adviser said Bangladesh missions abroad are short of staff, citing Qatar: a mission that has to distribute 300 passports cannot provide other services, and even a person sent as a night guard is made to stamp passports; a decision has been taken to increase mission manpower.

The Foreign Adviser said passport services need to be digitised so that people do not have to come to the mission, and the passport reaches the applicant once correct documents are submitted; this was stated as an aim, not an existing service.
The Foreign Adviser said that Bangladeshis are the largest number among those who drown trying to cross the Mediterranean, and that this damages the country's image.

headline_en: Integrated online attestation system inaugurated
summary_en: On Wednesday 29 January 2025 the Foreign Adviser inaugurated an integrated online attestation system under the Apostille Convention 1961 at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. Students and professionals going abroad apply on the MyGov portal; the issuing authority, the controlling ministry and then the foreign ministry attest online and an e-Apostille certificate is downloaded, removing the need for attestation at foreign embassies in Dhaka, which charge BDT 3,000 to 20,000 per page. Documents attested this way will currently be accepted in 117 countries.

facts.statement: Bangladesh inaugurated an integrated online attestation system on 29 January 2025 to replace manual attestation of certificates for students, professionals and others going or living abroad; attestation is done under the Apostille Convention 1961, to which Bangladesh has acceded, and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs issues an Apostille certificate as the attestation of a public document.
facts.source_in_article: the article; inauguration by Foreign Adviser Md. Touhid Hossain

facts.statement: The Apostille Convention 1961 currently has 127 party countries, but documents attested from Bangladesh will at present be accepted in 117 countries.
With an Apostille certificate, applicants will not need attestation from foreign embassies or, after travelling, from authorities in the destination country.

Under the manual system, academic certificates and other documents had to be attested by the issuing body, several authorities and the ministry concerned, then the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, then the foreign embassy in Dhaka, and after travel by the destination country's foreign ministry and authorities; for countries with no embassy in Dhaka, applicants had to travel to the neighbouring country whose embassy is concurrently accredited to Bangladesh.

Foreign embassies in Dhaka charge a service fee of BDT 3,000 to BDT 20,000 per page to attest a document; once the apostille programme is implemented this embassy fee will not be needed, saving Bangladeshi citizens an estimated BDT 500 to 700 crore a year.

To get an e-Apostille, students and professionals going abroad apply online on the MyGov portal (printed as মাইগভডটজিওভি); the issuing authority verifies and attests the document and sends it to its controlling ministry, which counter-attests and sends it online to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, which counter-attests under the convention and issues an e-Apostille certificate online.

When the Ministry of Foreign Affairs completes attestation, a notification goes to the applicant's registered mobile number, and the applicant downloads the e-Apostille certificate by clicking the 'Download' button on the personal dashboard of the MyGov portal.

During manual attestation of hard copies at government offices, applicants stand in long queues and fall into the hands of brokers, and forged seals and signatures are used; the article says the apostille programme is expected to remove brokers/middlemen and forged attestation.

headline_en: One arrested at Shah Amanat airport on human trafficking charge
summary_en: Airport immigration police arrested Iftekharul Alam of Fazilpur, Feni at Chattogram's Shah Amanat International Airport on the night of Saturday 11 January 2025, on information from National Security Intelligence, as he tried to fly to Dubai. He faces a case at the human trafficking tribunal in Cumilla and another filed on 11 January at Brahmanpara police station.

facts.statement: Immigration police at Shah Amanat International Airport, Chattogram arrested Iftekharul Alam of Fazilpur, Feni on a human trafficking charge on the night of 11 January 2025, acting on National Security Intelligence (NSI) information, as he tried to leave for Dubai on a Biman Bangladesh Airlines flight at 8:50 pm.
facts.source_in_article: airport authorities; airport public relations officer Mohammad Ibrahim Khalil

facts.statement: Iftekharul Alam has a case against him at the Human Trafficking Offences Suppression Tribunal-2, District and Sessions Judge, Cumilla, and a case under the Prevention and Suppression of Human Trafficking Act filed on 11 January at Brahmanpara police station, Cumilla; Chattogram airport immigration police have also submitted a case FIR against him.
facts.source_in_article: airport authorities; public relations officer Mohammad Ibrahim Khalil
